dialect.detail: Microsoft COBOL 3 for MS-DOS (SOURCE-COMPUTER MS-COBOL-3, OBJECT-COMPUTER MS-DOS); uses SCREEN SECTION with BLANK SCREEN, REVERSE-VIDEO, AUTO, AUTO-SKIP, and ACCEPT/DISPLAY with AT LINE/COLUMN syntax typical of MS-COBOL

purpose.domain_detail: Classic BASIC-to-COBOL port of the Creative Computing checkers game
purpose.summary: Implements a two-player checkers game where the computer plays X and the human plays O on an 8x8 board. The computer calculates moves using a simple scoring heuristic, handles jumps and king promotions, and displays the board on a CRT screen. This is a port of the Creative Computing BASIC checkers program to Microsoft COBOL for MS-DOS.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with full-screen CRT I/O
ACCEPT/DISPLAY with AT LINE COLUMN positioning
SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE for signed numeric data
REDEFINES used to initialize board from a string literal
Heavy use of GOTO (24 occurrences) reflecting BASIC-style control flow
PERFORM VARYING with AFTER for nested loops
No EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS, no COPY statements
verdict.notes: This is clearly a port of the Creative Computing BASIC checkers game (evidenced by the 'CREATIVE COMPUTING MORRISTOWN, NEW JERSEY' banner and line-number comments like 000005, 000065, etc. matching BASIC line numbers). The MS-COBOL-3 / MS-DOS identifiers confirm the Microsoft COBOL 3.x dialect for DOS. The heavy use of GOTO and line-number comments are artifacts of the BASIC-to-COBOL translation style.
